title: 초성 ㄱ·ㅋ·ㄲ 소리 구별하고 읽기
summary: Practice distinguishing and pronouncing initial ㄱ (plain), ㅋ (aspirated), and ㄲ (tense). Use clear English sound anchors: ㄱ ≈ a light sound between English g and k, ㅋ ≈ the k in “key,” ㄲ = tense “kk” with no exact English match. Read and choose simple words that begin with these letters.
objective: Beginner learners will accurately hear and pronounce ㄱ (plain), ㅋ (aspirated), and ㄲ (tense) in word-initial position, connect them to helpful English sound references (ㄱ ≈ between English g and k, with a light puff of air, ㅋ ≈ k in “key,” ㄲ = tense “kk,” no exact English equivalent), and correctly read and select simple words containing these initials.
exercises: Choose the word that begins with ㅋ (aspirated): 가게 / 코 / 꽃
Read the romanization and choose the matching Korean word: kkoma → 가방 / 꼬마 / 카메라
Choose the word that begins with ㄱ (plain): 콩 / 껌 / 고기
Match each word to its first consonant: 꼬마, 가방, 코 → [ㄱ], [ㅋ], [ㄲ]
Match each English hint to the word whose first sound fits it: between 'g' and 'k' (light puff) / 'k' in "key" / tense 'kk' → Choices: 꽃, 가게, 카메라
answers: between g and k→가게, key→카메라, kk→꽃

letters.sound: Plain (lax) consonant. The back of the tongue lightly closes against the soft palate, then releases. At the start of a word, a light puff of air comes out: weaker than ㅋ and softer than ㄲ.
Aspirated consonant. Same tongue position as ㄱ, but released with a strong puff of air.
Tense consonant. Same tongue position as ㄱ, but the throat and tongue are tensed and the sound is released sharply, with no puff of air.
